reconcile.note: Henry insists the lily saying forbids anxious care, not ordinary labor, since idleness tempts God while diligence still fulfills our duty to provide.

discrepancy.note: Remsburg presses the same rhetorical question the household codes answer differently: did Jesus actually teach industry and frugality.

quotes.text: What did he teach? Did he advocate industry and frugality? “Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth” (Matthew vi, 19). “Take no thought for your life what ye shall eat or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on” (25). “Take therefore no thought for the morrow” (34).
quotes.attr: John E. Remsburg (d. 1919), The Christ: A Critical Review and Analysis of the Evidences of His Existence (1909), sec. on the moral teachings of Jesus, on Matthew 6:34.

sides.verseText: Therefore don't be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day's own evil is sufficient.

sides.snippet: if anyone doesn't provide for his own, and especially his own household, he has denied the faith, and is worse than an unbeliever
sides.verseText: But if anyone doesn't provide for his own, and especially his own household, he has denied the faith, and is worse than an unbeliever.
